name: DynCap
audience: people who make Shorts, Reels and TikToks, and freelance editors who caption videos in Premiere Pro
oneLiner: Animated word-by-word captions for your videos, made on your own Windows PC. No subscription.
facts: A Windows 10/11 desktop app that adds animated word-by-word captions to videos.
You open a video or audio file, it turns the speech into words timed to when you say them, and you fix any wrong word like editing a document.
Transcription runs on your own PC, so your video is not uploaded anywhere. The speech model downloads once (about 480 MB) the first time.
A 1-minute clip transcribes in under a minute. Making a 60-second captioned video takes about 2 to 3 minutes.
Exports either a finished .mp4 with captions and audio, ready to post, or a transparent .mov overlay to put on V2 in Premiere Pro.
Works with any Premiere Pro version because it is a separate app, not a plugin. You do not need Premiere: the .mp4 export is a finished video.
There is a live preview with sound before you export.
The free version has 3 caption styles (Bold Pop, Clean Subtitle, Minimal White), both export types, no watermark and no time limit.

Pro costs $19 once, with no subscription. It adds all 9 styles, your own animations (fade, blur, slide, scale, per phrase or per word), keyword highlights in their own colour with emoji, and saved presets. A Pro key works on 2 PCs.

Bold Pop: big uppercase words, the spoken word turns yellow and pops. Clean Subtitle: the sentence on a dark box, words light up as they are spoken. Karaoke Box: a box jumps to each word. Neon Glow: glowing letters that slide up.
Max words on screen sets the pace: 1 to 3 words feels punchy, 5 to 8 reads like subtitles.
Hindi, Marathi and Nepali come out in proper Devanagari script, and about 90 other languages work too.
It can also save a plain .srt subtitle file, for example for YouTube.
Many caption tools and plugins charge a monthly fee, often $10 to $30 a month.
dont: Do not say it works on Mac, phones or in the browser. It is Windows only.
Do not say it is a Premiere Pro plugin or panel, or that it edits, cuts or trims your video.
Do not say it is fully offline without saying the speech model downloads once first.
Do not say it translates captions into another language, or that it is perfectly accurate.
Do not name or criticise other caption apps by name.
